conventions.source: docs/CONTRACT_V42.md section AK, design docs/v42_plan.md section 5 (balloon loops, consist, stops).
conventions.anchor: normalised [ax, ay] of the full untrimmed frame = world origin. Train cars: the ground point under the car centre on the track centre line. Loop decals: the turnout point T1 = L(-1, 0) / T2 = L(37, 0) (anchorPx is exact; place the frame so anchorPx lands on anchorWorldPx). Fence tile: the segment middle on the fence line. Props: the ground under the post / tower centre.
conventions.train: characters{} kind "train" (same as assets/town): rendered dirs S, SE, E, NE, N + flipX mirrors (SW <- SE, W <- E, NW <- NE); frame names {anim}_{dir}_{i}; anims idle (1 f), move (8 f, one wheel turn at 45 deg / frame + a gentle sway; the game sets the fps from the speed: fps = 12 * v / 2.6 like the engine, or per car 8 * v / trackPerLoopM for slip-free wheels), door_open (box car only, SE + NE only, 4 f once; play it reversed to close, then idle). anims[a].dirs lists the dirs an anim exists in. shadowFrames: a soft ground shadow for each of the 8 headings (NOT mirrored: the light does not flip) with its own frameSize / anchor; draw it on the ground layer under the car, then the car.
conventions.coupling: couplerM = the coupler faces in metres along the heading (front negative). The cars touch at the couplers: anchor spacing = couplerM.back of the car in front - couplerM.front of the car behind (trainConsist.*.spacingM). The dark gap between two bodies = the two coupler stubs (0.15 m each).
conventions.points: every *Point / *Points / cargoSlots value is a px offset [dx, dy] from the car anchor for the rendered dir; for a mirrored dir negate dx and swap L <-> R. doorPoints[dir] = {L: [front, rear], R: [front, rear]} = ground beside each door (coach: the platform steps; box car: the two door halves); L / R = left / right of the car facing its heading. windowPoints = lit window centres visible in that dir (night glow), lampPoints = lanterns / tail lamps, cargoPoint = [dx, dy, behind] inside the open box car door (where crates fly in), cargoSlots = 6 x [dx, dy, behind] bottom-centre of each crate stack on the flat car deck (sorted back to front: draw in this order), stackStep px per crate icon at cargoScale. headTop = top of the roof (min over dirs; headTopDir per dir).
conventions.decals: rail_loop_ours / rail_loop_town are ground decals (bake them into the ground like the rail tiles, AFTER the straight rail_x tiles listed in tilesUnder, which must be drawn as plain rail_x - no buffer stop at k -6 / 41). They are a difference matte against exactly those tiles: decal over tiles = the loop, the turnout (repainted straight route) and a seamless joint at A / T. The straight main line between A and the turnout is NOT in the decal (the tiles show through).
conventions.tiles: rail_fence_x: one tile = sqrt(2) m along world X, step (64, 32) px, owns the post at its -X end, shadows join seamlessly; close a run with rail_fence_x_end at the +X end. Depth-sort with the actors (tileLayer "objects").
conventions.shadows: decals / fence / props have a baked soft cool shadow falling screen down-right; train cars none (use their shadowFrames).

atlases.notes: the flat car + the live props of both loops (rail_fence_x / _end, rail_switch_stand, rail_water_tower): resident with the train

ground decals only (rail_loop_ours / rail_loop_town): bake them into the ground with the rail_x tiles, then release the page (RoadPaint BAKE_ONLY). Keep it lossless (no WebP / palette): the decal is an exact difference matte over the tiles.

rail_switch_stand.notes: beside the switch toe on the land side at the end of the two tie bars, on the fence line (j -0.75): walkers on the 역 가는 길 (j -1) pass it like the fence; keep a blockM radius free of walkers

rail_water_tower.notes: optional; BEHIND the loop on the sea side (not in the infield: there it hid the cars rounding the loop). Every track point under its body is drawn in front of it; its footprint >= 60 px on land, >= 0.7 cell from the ballast (checked by tr2_check / train2_phaser)

rail_loop_ours.notes: Balloon loop at 서리역 (rail_loop_ours): the spring turnout at [-1, 0] (long switch ties, switch blades + two tie bars reaching to the land side, closure rails, frog and guard rails; the straight route through the turnout is repainted), curves D -> T and C -> D (R 1.75 cells), the straight B -> C and the semicircle A -> B joining the straight main line at A. Same ballast / sleepers / rails / snow / shadow as rail_x. Draw on the ground layer AFTER the rail_x tiles in tilesUnder (plain rail_x, drawn exactly as RoadPaint draws them); pathPx = the loop centre line T -> D -> C -> B -> A in px from the anchor (for RailPath cross-checks).

rail_switch_stand.notes: beside the switch toe on the land side at the end of the two tie bars, on the fence line (j -0.75): walkers on the 역 가는 길 (j -1) pass it like the fence; keep a blockM radius free of walkers

rail_water_tower.notes: optional; BEHIND the loop on the sea side (not in the infield: there it hid the cars rounding the loop). Every track point under its body is drawn in front of it; its footprint >= 60 px on land, >= 0.7 cell from the ballast (checked by tr2_check / train2_phaser)

rail_loop_town.notes: Balloon loop at 솔방울역 (rail_loop_town): the spring turnout at [37, 0] (long switch ties, switch blades + two tie bars reaching to the land side, closure rails, frog and guard rails; the straight route through the turnout is repainted), curves D -> T and C -> D (R 1.75 cells), the straight B -> C and the semicircle A -> B joining the straight main line at A. Same ballast / sleepers / rails / snow / shadow as rail_x. Draw on the ground layer AFTER the rail_x tiles in tilesUnder (plain rail_x, drawn exactly as RoadPaint draws them); pathPx = the loop centre line T -> D -> C -> B -> A in px from the anchor (for RailPath cross-checks).

rail_fence_x.notes: Low snow fence tile along world X (one grid cell = sqrt(2) m, step (64, 32) px): weathered wooden posts with snow caps and two plank rails with snow on top, a little drift at the foot (~0.6 m). The tile owns the post at its -X end; chain tiles at stepPx and close the run with rail_fence_x_end (the post at the +X end of the last tile). Shadows join seamlessly (partition-of-unity cut like the rails). Depth-sort with the actors by anchor y (it hides the lower wheels of a train standing behind it).

ours.notes: plan 5.1: j -0.75, i -6 .. -1.5 (4 tiles + the closing post; a 5th tile at i -1.5 would reach the switch toe)

rail_fence_x_end.notes: Closing post of a rail_fence_x run (place it at the +X end of the last tile = last tile anchor + (32, 16) px).

rail_switch_stand.notes: Switch stand of the spring turnout (~0.9 m): two timber blocks, a black post with a red-and-white weighted throw lever at its foot and a lamp box on top. idle_0 = lamp green (set for the straight route, lever down to the left), idle_1 = lamp yellow (the train trails through, lever thrown). The game flips them with sfx_switch_clack; lampPoint = lens centre (night glow).

rail_water_tower.notes: Small wooden water tower beside the loop (footprint 1.6 m, ~3.2 m): four braced timber legs, a round stave tank with iron hoops, a cone roof with snow, a ladder and a swinging spout. idle = spout raised; pour_base = spout lowered (no water); anim pour (6 f loop) = the water stream with drips and a splash in the trough, shipped as small OVERLAY frames drawn over pour_base (same origin).
rail_water_tower.usage: idle: show frame. Pouring: set the tower sprite to pourBase (spout lowered) and play anim pour on a second sprite at the same position, origin and depth (+0.001): the pour frames are small trimmed overlays (water stream, drips, splash) whose sourceSize = frameSize, so they land exactly. Back to idle: hide the overlay, show frame.

shadowFrames.notes: Soft ground shadow for each of the 8 headings (NOT mirrored: the light does not flip). Draw it under the car at the same position (ground layer), then the car.

train_coach.notes: 객차 "솔방울호" passenger coach (3.0 m over the couplers, body 2.7 m, 1.25 x 1.85 m): sky-blue lower body with a gold pinecone emblem and a blank gold name plate mid-side, cream window band with thin gold lines, a slate-teal barrel roof with a snow cap and little vents (never red: it must not continue the engine cab), 4 big warm-lit windows per side with 2-3 seated toy passengers each (bobble hats, earmuffs, scarves; two of them wave), open end platforms with gold railings, steps on both sides and a lantern at each end, dark bogies with red disc wheels. idle = standing (1 f); move = 8-frame loop: one wheel turn (45 deg / frame), a gentle body sway, the wavers wave. doorPoints = ground beside the platform steps (L/R x front/rear) where passengers step on / off; windowPoints = lit window centres (night glow); lampPoints = the two end lanterns.

nightGlow.notes: one fv_glow per windowPoints entry at windowK and per lampPoints entry at lampK; endWindowPoints (the end-door window between two coupled coaches) stay dark (0) or at most 0.15 on the last coach - stacked with both lanterns they make a white blob at every coupling. Hidden lamps are not listed.

shadowFrames.notes: Soft ground shadow for each of the 8 headings (NOT mirrored: the light does not flip). Draw it under the car at the same position (ground layer), then the car.

train_boxcar.notes: 화물칸 box car (2.6 m over the couplers, body 2.3 m, 1.3 x 1.9 m): warm chestnut planks, a cream X-brace on each half of the sliding door (two leaves) on both sides, a dark green barrel roof with a plank roof walkway and a snow cap, an end ladder, a cream pinecone-crate pictogram (no text) beside the door, red-brown underframe, dark bogies with red disc wheels. idle / move closed; door_open (SE, NE, 4 f once; the game plays it reversed to close) slides both leaves apart and shows the crates and sacks inside under a warm lamp. doorPoints = ground beside each door half (where crates fly in); cargoPoint = the floor just inside the open door.

doorAnim.notes: stopped headings only (SE / NE, mirrored NW / SW); frame 3 = fully open

shadowFrames.notes: Soft ground shadow for each of the 8 headings (NOT mirrored: the light does not flip). Draw it under the car at the same position (ground layer), then the car.

train_flatcar.notes: 무개화차 flat car (2.4 m over the couplers, body 2.1 m, 1.3 x 0.75 m, deck 0.55 m): dark oiled-wood plank deck, red-brown side sills with stake pockets and 6 low stakes per side, iron corner plates, a rolled green tarp lashed with rope + a rope coil at the rear end, a small red tail lamp at each end, a little snow at the edges; the middle of the deck is EMPTY: the game stacks crate icons (lgx items at cargoScale, stackStep px apart) on cargoSlots (2 rows x 3, bottom-centre of each stack on the deck, sorted back to front). idle 1 f, move 8 f (wheel turn + gentle sway).

nightGlow.notes: red tail lamps: fv_glow at lampK, tinted; hidden lamps are not listed.

train_flatcar.cargoIcons: lgx_items crate / box icons (item_crate_*, cardboard_box_*), origin [0.5, 0.75], drawn at cargoScale, k-th icon of a stack at (dx, dy - k * stackStep)

pageRule.keep: every shadow_* and every frame that is not {anim}_{dir}_{i} (the props); the stopped headings NE / SE in full (idle, move 0-7, door_open 0-3); the curve dirs S / E / N: move 0, 2, 4, 6 + idle_0 (an alias of move_0)
pageRule.notes: tools/build/pack_pages.py TRAIN rule (v42-dirs-1) extended to the train2 fragment; budget.*.pageMiB is that page, packed with pack_pages.pack

engineFlip.notes: the town engine is not symmetric about its anchor (ax 0.434): Phaser mirrors a frame about its middle, so a flipped engine with origin ax sits 28 px off its track point. The train2 cars are packed symmetric (ax 0.5) and need nothing.

curvePlacement.anchor: chord midpoint: draw each car at the midpoint of its bogie chord P(s - 0.4 L) .. P(s + 0.4 L) (not at the arc point P(s)); on the R 1.75-cell loop curves the arc point lies ~0.3 m outside the chord, which pushes neighbouring cars apart sideways (folded coaches, a coach beside the engine on the S-curve)
curvePlacement.heading: the chord angle -> nearest of 8 headings with ~8 deg hysteresis (keep the current heading until the chord is more than 22.5 + 8 deg away from it)
curvePlacement.shadow: the shadow of the chosen heading at the same (chord midpoint) position
curvePlacement.notes: validated in tools/test/train2_phaser.mjs (placement "chord", the loop GIFs and tr2_loop_curve_cmp.png compare it with the arc-point placement)

trainConsist.notes: spacingM = anchor-to-anchor along the track (back coupler of the car in front - front coupler of the car behind); lengthM = nose (engine front coupler) to tail (last back coupler). train_engine lives in assets/town; its manifest says couplerM.back 1.22 but its sprite draws the rear coupler hook out to 1.375 m behind its anchor (cab rear at 1.28 m), so with the plan figure 2.72 m the engine and the first car overlap and no gap shows. Use couplerOverride (spacingM[0] = 2.875 m, +0.155 m, the train 0.155 m longer); spacingPlanM / lengthPlanM keep the plan section 5.2 figures. Between the new cars the visible gap is the two coupler stubs, >= 0.3 m.
